title: Claudex Loop skill: four-phase (Recon, Interrogate, Review, Build) workflow where Claude Code plans and OpenAI Codex adversarially reviews the plan and the final diff, so neither model grades its own work

tools.name: Claudex Loop
tools.detail: GitHub repo (README banner 'CLAUDEX LOOP - two models - one argument - zero echo chamber'), MIT license, badges 'Claude Code skill + plugin' and 'OpenAI Codex adversarial reviewer'; link in creator's bio

tools.name: OpenAI Codex
tools.detail: reviews PLAN.md in a read-only sandbox, returns VERDICT: APPROVED or REVISE; optional codex-build

claims: AI systems grade their own work favorably; a second model closes the echo chamber
Works on greenfield and brownfield projects

Phase 0 Recon: scouts the codebase/docs or researches the web; Phase 1 Interrogate: 'much deeper version of plan mode', one load-bearing question at a time, veto-by-exception; Phase 2 Review: Codex reviews PLAN.md read-only, rounds continue until APPROVED, Claude arbitrates findings; Phase 3 Build (optional): Claude or Codex builds, then the other model cross-inspects the diff against the plan
Artifacts per run: PLAN.md (the what) and PLAN-REVIEW-LOG.md (the full round-by-round path)
Invariant: 'whoever made the thing never checks the thing'; Codex is read-only during review and never touches a file
README anecdote: first real run of a solo-creator CRM - a rival model found one unbuildable subsystem and six designs that would have corrupted data before any code existed
how_to_steps: Install the Claudex Loop skill/plugin in Claude Code (link in bio)
Tell it what you want -> Recon
Claude writes PLAN.md; Codex reviews; iterate until both approve
Build with Claude (or Codex); the other model inspects the diff; findings arbitrated and logged

relevance.why: A structured, tool-enforced second-model review of plans and diffs is exactly the quality gate a solo founder lacks; uses subscriptions Haji may already have (Claude Max + ChatGPT/Codex).

implement_score.why: Install a skill, run on the next feature; the plan-review-before-code loop is cheap and the PLAN-REVIEW-LOG gives an audit trail. Cost is Codex quota and slower kickoff on small tasks - use only for non-trivial features.
